items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: I went to a club in Chicago called the Beehive. And a friend of mine was there. He was working with Clifford Brown. And we went and heard him

ctx.x: Yeah. Oh we had his records you know. I mean he was like a teenager himself when I first heard him, when he first started playing all these things. But the first time I heard him — I’ll show you how sensitive he was — I went to a club in Chicago called the Beehive. And a friend of mine was there. He was working with Clifford Brown. And we went and heard him and Clifford was watching the audience when he wasn’t — Max was playing, and Max was playing kind of loud. And this friend of mine, I’m watching the stage all…

I love this comment you made about when you had, it might have been M’Boom that you were talking about or some of the other large ensembles, but you said something about, “Everyone has a different idea of where the beat is at.” And I can imagine that’s got to be a little tricky.
